en: The Sūtra on the Great Dhāraṇī of Parṇaśavarī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Da Fu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Imperial Subject Dharma-xian, the Great Master Mingjiao, by imperial decree: At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying,
"I observe that among the immeasurable sentient beings in the world,
many commit sinful karma and fall into the evil realms."
Only after an immeasurable period of time will they finally attain liberation;
even if they are born as humans, their limbs may be incomplete,
and even if they do possess them in full, they will have meager merit and little wisdom.
Constantly, evil Māras and malevolent ghosts and spirits will seek opportunities during day and night to afflict them in various ways, preventing them from attaining peace and security.
Out of compassion for such beings, I shall preach this great *dhāraṇī*, the Parṇaśavarī.
It expels evil Māras and malevolent spirits.
If there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī and,
with a heart of utmost sincerity, receive, uphold, recite, and chant it, and offer worship and reverence to it.
May those evil Māras and malevolent spirits be driven far away;
may calamities be eliminated and all epidemics cease,
so that wherever they dwell, there shall be peace, security, and happiness.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo 'ryāmitābhāya tathāgatāya.* (1) Homage to the Triple Gem.
(2) Homage to the Noble Amitābha Tathāgata. (3) To the Tathāgata.
1. Arhaṭe 2. Samyak-saṃbuddhāya 3. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya 4. Bodhisattvāya 5. Mahāsattvāya 6. Mahākāruṇikāya
Gāye bha namaḥ mahāsattvārambhadapradāpadāya moditasattvāya mahāsattvāya vāmanitunamo 'kṣa.

Having heard the World-Honored One speak this dhāraṇī, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, please do not have any concern;
I shall remember and uphold it, and cause it to circulate throughout the world."
"May all sentient beings obtain great and wholesome benefit.
Having spoken these words, he immediately prostrated with his head at the feet of the World-Honored One and withdrew with joy.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Great Dhāraṇī of Parṇaśavarī.
